summary: self-certificates ships a double-base64 dropper in test/key.pem that fetches and executes a remote payload via python3
details: The package presents itself as a self-signed certificate helper but stages a hidden dropper. index.js reads test/key.pem, strips the PEM markers, and base64-decodes the body; the decoded bytes are a second PEM-wrapped base64 blob that yields a JavaScript IIFE. That decoded string is passed as the `default_format` argument to `selfsign.generate` from the declared dependency `self-sign@^5.6.3`, where it is executed. The IIFE fetches https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php and pipes the response body into a detached `python3` process (falling back to `python` on win32) via stdin, with `windowsHide:true`. The chain triggers whenever the advertised `generateCertificates` API is invoked, giving the operator of aptupdate.org arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine. The disguise of the payload as an RSA private key under test/ and the double base64 encoding are cover for the layered dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
